title: The ladder: one axis per rung, exit criteria, and a reference rung
purpose: Write the ladder as overlays that change one axis each, decide from measured evidence whether a rung may be climbed, account for what each rung spent, and keep a small reference run that repeats on a schedule.

steps.display: python ladder.py check recipes/ladder/*.yaml   # an overlay may change only the settings of the axis it declares
steps.output:
rung1-recipe.yaml        ok   rung 1 defines the starting recipe
rung2-length.yaml        ok   changes only ['MAX_COMPLETION', 'THINKING'], all of axis 'length'
rung3-model-size.yaml    ok   changes only ['MODEL'], all of axis 'model_size'
bad-two-axes.yaml        REFUSED declares axis 'length' but also changes ['MODEL'] (axes ['length', 'model_size'])

steps.display: python ladder.py gate rung1-recipe   # may the team climb to rung 2?
steps.output:
decision: HOLD
  HOLD  curve fit: 2 x std of the ceiling        wanted <= 0.03  measured 0.295
  PASS  unexplained waiting, share of step       wanted <= 0.1   measured 0.000
  PASS  restart from a checkpoint tested         wanted yes      measured True

steps.display: python ladder.py gate rung2-length   # may the team climb to rung 3?
steps.output:
decision: HOLD
  HOLD  curve fit: 2 x std of the ceiling        wanted <= 0.03  measured None
  PASS  unexplained waiting, share of step       wanted <= 0.1   measured 0.030
  PASS  restart from a checkpoint tested         wanted yes      measured True

steps.display: python ladder.py spend   # GPU hours each rung used, against its budget (three GPUs, evaluation left out)
steps.output:
rung 1  recipe        0.89 of 2.0 GPU hours  (3 runs)
rung 2  length        0.21 of 1.0 GPU hours  (1 run)

steps.display: kubectl -n rl-scale get lws rollout   # 2 engine(s), settings: defaults
kubectl apply -f reference-rung.yaml   # a CronJob that repeats a 20-step run every night against the current code and image
steps.output:
NAME             SCHEDULE    TIMEZONE   SUSPEND   ACTIVE   LAST SCHEDULE   AGE
reference-rung   0 3 * * *   <none>     False     0        <none>          1s

steps.display: kubectl create job reference-manual --from=cronjob/reference-rung   # the schedule's run, started by hand
python reference.py reference-1123-1006   # compare the 20 steps with the same 20 steps of the S02 run
steps.output:
mean reward, reference vs baseline: differs by 0.030
seconds per step: differs by 16%
verdict: within tolerance

checks.description: rungs 2 and 3 each change one axis, and an overlay that changes two is refused
checks.because: A rung that changes the answer length and the model together cannot say which one caused a regression. The launcher refuses it before anything is scheduled.

checks.description: the gate returns a decision with the measured value of every criterion, for both rungs
checks.because: The criteria are the design's own: the ceiling's confidence interval, the unexplained waiting, and a tested restart. Each value comes from a run in this session.

checks.description: a rung whose curve is not known is held: the 20-step thinking run cannot support a ceiling estimate
checks.because: A fit needs points past the curve's midpoint. A short run at a new length has none, so the gate says so instead of guessing.

checks.description: each rung stayed within its declared budget
checks.because: A rung's budget is part of its overlay, so the cost of the ladder is known before it starts and checked after.

checks.description: the reference run completed and matches its baseline within tolerance
checks.because: Same recipe, same code, same images, twenty steps. If a library upgrade changes the training dynamics or the step time, this run moves before a large one does.

checks.description: the comparison flags a run whose reward or time per step has moved (made-up perturbations of the baseline)
checks.because: A tolerance that never fires is no check. The same function is applied to the baseline against itself (quiet), to a copy with a reward 0.3 higher (flagged), and to a copy with three more seconds per step (flagged).
